metadata.title: Mason Rudolph listed as Steelers' QB2 on Week 1 depth chart
metadata.description: The Steelers have listed Mason Rudolph as their QB2 on the Week 1 depth chart.
metadata.analysis: Will Howard is No. 3 and rookie Drew Allar is No. 4 on the opening depth chart as the Steelers kept all four quarterbacks on the roster.

metadata.title: Mason Rudolph - DNP on Thursday
metadata.description: Rudolph did not play in Thursday night's preseason finale against the Bills.
metadata.analysis: Rudolph has likely already secured the backup quarterback role behind Aaron Rodgers to start the 2026 regular season. Thursday night's contest once again saw a half of Will Howard (head) and a half of Drew Allar at quarterback, leaving Rudolph to rest with Rodgers as they await the regular season.

metadata.title: Mason Rudolph - Likely finished for preseason
metadata.description: Rudolph will not play in Friday's preseason game against the Jets, Chris Adamski of TribLive.com reports.
metadata.analysis: Coach Mike McCarthy said Wednesday that he "saw what I need to see from Mason last week," implying the veteran quarterback has a place on the team for 2026. Friday's game will be dominated by Will Howard and Drew Allar, one of whom is presumably the Steelers' quarterback of the future once Aaron Rodgers retires.

metadata.title: Mason Rudolph Sharp in Preseason Start
metadata.description: Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Mason Rudolph completed 10 of 11 pass attempts for 93 yards in a 28-9 preseason victory over the Green Bay Packers. Rudolph got off to a rocky start, taking two sacks over his first four snaps, but quickly settled in and led the offense down the field on its second possession. Although the Steelers were unable to score after an offensive holding penalty nullified a three-yard rushing touchdown by Lew Nichols, Rudolph displayed early chemistry with rookie wideout Germie Bernard and several other pass-catchers throughout the drive. The 31-year-old then gave way to second-year pro Will Howard and rookie signal-caller Drew Allar, both of whom also impressed. It will be interesting to see how Pittsburgh's quarterback depth chart shakes out entering the regular season, with all three players competing for backup duties behind Aaron Rodgers. Rudolph is likely to see additional preseason action next weekend against the New York Jets.

metadata.title: Mason Rudolph Dominating Steelers' Backup Competition
metadata.description: The Pittsburgh Steelers spent a third and a sixth-round pick at quarterback over the course of the past two drafts, but according to beat reporter Alan Saunders, the battle for the primary backup job behind Aaron Rodgers has been dominated by veteran Mason Rudolph. Saunders lists both Will Howard and Drew Allar among his losers of the second week of Steelers training camp, with them all but handing the competition to Rudolph. While Rudolph himself has done little to stand out, Howard has reportedly been unable to close the gap that looked to be tightening during OTAs, making too many errors to overcome a limited skill set. Allar, meanwhile, has flashed standout athleticism, but is still a long way away from running an NFL offense after a near-total teardown of his fundamentals. With Rodgers preparing for his 22nd and final season, the rookie still has the best chances to eventually take over, but the backup job for 2026 is expected to remain with Rudolph.

metadata.title: Mason Rudolph - Set for share of quarterback reps
metadata.description: Rudolph is set to receive a fair share of the quarterback reps during training camp, Mike DeFabo of The Athletic reports.
metadata.analysis: Rudolph received reps in the two-minute drill Tuesday, outperforming starter Aaron Rodgers and gaining an opportunity that Will Howard and Drew Allar did not have. The 31-year-old veteran quarterback continues to separate as the clear No. 2, and with Aaron Rodgers already declaring 2026 his retirement season, it is reasonable to assume that Rudolph could see some regular-season action.

metadata.title: Mason Rudolph to start off training camp taking second-team reps
metadata.description: Steelers coach Mike McCarthy said Mason Rudolph will start off taking reps with the second-team.
metadata.analysis: Will Howard and Drew Allar will split the reps with the No. 3 team. They'll likely all continue to compete throughout training camp and into the preseason.

metadata.title: Mason Rudolph - Out of 2026 starting mix
metadata.description: Rudolph will be relegated to a backup role again in 2026, as Aaron Rodgers signed a one-year contract with the Steelers on Monday.
metadata.analysis: Rodgers will reclaim the starting role he possessed in 2025, leaving Rudolph to battle for the second spot on the depth chart with 2025 sixth-round pick Will Howard and 2026 third-round pick Drew Allar (ankle). If one of the younger quarterbacks shows promise in training camp, the Steelers could also opt to trade Rudolph to a team seeking an experienced backup. Rudolph has posted a 9-9-1 record in 19 regular-season starts split between the Steelers and Titans, including a loss in his lone start of 2025 with Pittsburgh while Rodgers was sidelined by a wrist injury.

metadata.title: Mason Rudolph splitting reps to begin offseason program
metadata.description: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said QBs Mason Rudolph and Will Howard are splitting reps in the Steelers' offseason program.
metadata.analysis: Rudolph and Howard are currently leading the Steelers quarterback room with Aaron Rodgers still a free agent. It still seems very possible that Rodgers signs a deal with Pittsburgh at some point this offseason, but Howard and Rudolph will continue to see the reps for now.

metadata.title: Mason Rudolph - Sees limited action in 2025
metadata.description: Rudolph completed 38 of 52 passes for 310 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions while rushing seven times for six yards over five appearances during the 2025 regular season.
metadata.analysis: The bulk of Rudolph's playing time during the regular season came in the middle of the year, as he entered the team's Week 11 matchup against Cincinnati in relief after Aaron Rodgers got hurt before starting against the Bears in Week 12. Rudolph will remain under contract with the Steelers for the 2026 campaign, but it wouldn't be surprising to see the team bring in other options at quarterback if Aaron Rodgers retires during the offseason.
